narrative_purpose: Turns the four-tier method into a memorable physical sorting act: record, reasoned bridge, granted premise, and measured specimen occupy distinct trays and cannot silently trade places.
subject: Four shallow specimen trays arranged in one row on a dark examination table. The first tray holds a short strip of exposed motion-picture film with visible but unreadable image frames and a sealed archive tag with no writing. The second holds two matching broken stone halves joined by a carefully fitted narrow wooden bridge. The third holds one modest stone floating above an otherwise empty tray, tethered by exactly one luminous thread. The fourth holds a pinned glowing leaf beside a small glass measuring cylinder and brass calipers. Each tray is physically separate with a narrow dark gap around it.
scene: A quiet naturalist's evidence table viewed from above, bare except for the four deliberately sorted trays.
camera: Direct top-down view, all four trays fully visible and equal in size.
light: Low cool ambient with living light from the leaf and the single tether; a restrained amber glint on the calipers and film edge.
palette: Dark slate and stone neutrals under the global palette; cyan-teal glow confined to the speculative tether and living specimen; sparse amber metal highlights.
style: Painterly museum-study plate, tactile and orderly, with no infographic chrome.
detail_level: High detail within each tray, especially the film frames, fitted bridge, single tether and measuring tools; plain dark tabletop elsewhere.
composition: Four equal trays read left to right, with strong separation and open dark margins around every object for interface labels.
consistency_notes: The trays must remain distinct: recorded image strip, constructed bridge, exactly one tethered impossibility, and measured biological specimen. Never blend the contents across trays.
negative_prompt: no readable writing, no symbols, no arrows, no UI, no poster layout, no photographic or 3D-render look, no clutter, no fifth tray
